extracted.intended_audience: Imaging core facilities and imaging scientists at nonprofit universities or research institutes applying to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Imaging Scientists RFA
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Imaging Scientists RFA to fund an Imaging Scientist embedded in an imaging core (five-year award: initial 3 years + potential 2-year renewal). Includes eligibility, required application components, budget limits, formatting, and data/software sharing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goals and Imaging Scientist role expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Imaging Scientist should work at the interface of biology, microscopy hardware, and imaging software to increase interactions between biologists and technology experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful Imaging Programs will employ an Imaging Scientist who: (a) works collaboratively with experimental biologists on projects at the imaging core; (b) participates in courses that disseminate advanced microscopy methods and analysis; (c) trains students and postdocs in imaging technology; (d) participates in a network of CZI Imaging Scientists to identify needs and drive advances in the imaging field; (e) attends twice-yearly CZI scientific workshops and meetings. Imaging Scientists are expected to have expertise in either hardware or software, collaborate broadly with biologists at the home institution and interface with the local IT team, teach in at least one practical course advertised and open to external scientists, and evaluate and teach new analysis software to inexperienced users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by domestic and foreign non-profit organizations; public and private institutions such as colleges, universities, hospitals, laboratories, units of state and local government; and eligible agencies of the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imaging cores across the world may apply. CZI reserves the sole right to decide if an applicant and applicant organization meet eligibility requirements. Consult your institution for eligibility and institutional indirect cost policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must be the Imaging Scientist and currently employed at the applying institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The person submitting the application should be the Imaging Scientist, who must be currently employed at the institution submitting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Imaging Scientist’s Biosketch and Personal Statement must be provided. The Imaging Scientist details in the application must be completed and all required fields filled for that individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: One application per imaging core
rubrics_metrics.description: An imaging core may submit only one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different imaging cores from a single institution may submit separate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaging core should serve a broad community
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaging cores should serve a broad community of scientists at their institutions, not just a small number of labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must describe the user base and how the core serves the institution; see 'Accomplishments and Description of the Imaging Core' section for required details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable expertise: hardware or software
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaging Scientists should have expertise with either imaging hardware or software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are welcome from both medical and basic science imaging cores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity encouragement and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI encourages applications from underrepresented minorities, women, and early career scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facebook employees, including employees of any subsidiary Facebook entities, are not permitted to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional sign-off requirement (Institutional Approval Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must upload a signed Institutional Approval Form (Inst_Sign_off_form_Imaging_Sci_June_2020) as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form should be printed, reviewed, and signed by a person authorized to sign on behalf of your organization, agreeing to institutional and investigator commitments on data, resource sharing and publication policies. The field does not support encrypted documents or digital signatures; sign, scan, and upload as PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget caps and line-item limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum budget is $250,000 total costs per year for five years (no more than $1,250,000 total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No more than $200,000 per year may be requested for salary and fringe benefits of the Imaging Scientist, no more than $20,000 per year for teaching and travel expenses, and indirect costs limited to 15% of direct costs. Indirect costs cannot exceed 15% of direct costs and must be included within the annual budget total. Indirects may not be assessed on capital equipment or subcontracts; subcontractors may include up to 15% indirects of their direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget source and restriction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on acceptable sources of matching/additional salary funding and on travel for international grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If $200K is insufficient for salary, state proposed salary and explain additional funds sources. Funding from recharge or fee-for-service will not be accepted as the source of additional salary support. Restrictions may apply to international grantees using grant funds to travel to the U.S.; international grantees must use grant funds exclusively for activities conducted outside the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission platform and technical recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be completed and submitted through CZI’s grants management portal (SMApply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMApply is configured to work best using Google Chrome; familiarize with the portal well in advance. For technical assistance contact support@smapply.io or use the help ticket while logged in. Deadline extensions will not be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application structure and required tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The application consists of tasks: Imaging Scientist/Applicant Details (Part 1 and 2), Organization Details, Proposal Details, Imaging Core Details, and Project Proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required fields in each task. Many fields are required and must be completed exactly as requested (including tabular inputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD required
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID iD is required and must be entered in the format XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID identifiers will be used to streamline reporting. Contact sciencegrants@chanzuckerberg.com if you wish to opt out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement (Imaging Scientist) — limit 2 pages, concisely describe in four labeled sections: expertise and relevant experience; vision of how/what to teach biologists about modern imaging; vision about analysis and compute infrastructure needs in the next 10 years; vision for a single technical advance to drive the imaging field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should be prepared by the Imaging Scientist/Applicant. Note that CZI seeks experts who will do one-on-one support, liaise with IT, teach externally-advertised practical courses, and form a network to discuss advances. Max 2 pages; follow formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of the position statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of the Position — limit 0.5 page; describe the role the Imaging Scientist will play at the imaging core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepared by the Imaging Scientist/Applicant; keep within half-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch of the Imaging Scientist
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosketch — limit 5 pages; use NIH format or equivalent to describe education, employment, and identify up to five significant contributions (each described in ≤3 sentences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions may include publications (with DOI), preprints (with URL), shared datasets (with DOI), software (with DOI/reference), courses, patents, or other evidence. List selected authored publications and selected publications that acknowledge your contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch of the Core Director (if different)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Director biosketch — limit 5 pages; use NIH format or equivalent to describe education, employment, and evidence of productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill out this section if the Imaging Core Director is different from the applying Imaging Scientist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of software, analysis, and data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: One-page description listing heavily used acquisition and analysis software and describing analysis, compute, and data handling infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the software tools and how data and compute are handled; this should be concise (1 page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishments and description of the imaging core
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 5 pages describing whether core is service provider/research center/both, services offered and relative effort, user base (number of users) for the previous two years, and list of selected papers/patents/software from the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate lists for contributions authored by core staff and contributions that acknowledge the core. Describe frequency with which users acknowledge/cite the core. Provide links where possible. Discuss whether the service/research split is ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Proposal formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Proposal must be a single PDF with Table of Contents and bookmarks, numbered pages, at least 11-point font, margins ≥ 0.5 inch, no less than single-spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of Contents should list COVER PAGE; PERSONAL STATEMENT; VALUE OF THE POSITION; BIOSKETCH (Imaging Scientist); BIOSKETCH (Core Director); DESCRIPTION OF SOFTWARE AND DATA HANDLING; ACCOMPLISHMENTS OF THE IMAGING CORE; BUDGET; LETTER FROM THE DEAN OR CHAIR. Section 9 (Letter) must be prepared by Dean/Chair. Formatting and component requirements including word/page limits will be enforced; materials exceeding limits or not following requirements will not be considered during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Page — limit 1 page; provide on separate lines: title of program; university/institute name AND Tax ID; grant amount requested; proposed start date; name of Imaging Scientist AND email; name of Imaging Core Director; name of Dean or Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal title is limited to 75 characters in the portal. If needed, rename via application summary page controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget page and five-year budget submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget — limit 1 page; submit a budget for five years consistent with caps ($250K/year total; initial three-year period followed by potential two-year renewal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No more than $200K to salary and benefits of Imaging Scientist, no more than $20K to teaching/travel, and no more than 15% overhead. If proposing salary >$200K, explain additional funds source. Note: restrictions may apply to international grantees using funds to travel to the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter from the Dean or Chair requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter from the Dean/Chair — limit 2 pages; five separately labeled paragraphs describing: starting salary levels for Assistant/Associate/Full Professors (or equivalent); justification of applicant level; vision for imaging at the institution; how the imaging core is supported; plan to sustain candidate beyond five years. Must be signed and dated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section must be prepared by the Dean or Chair responsible for the Imaging Core and signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of formatting and page/word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The formatting and component requirements, including word and page limits indicated, will be enforced by the review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any submitted materials that exceed the word and page limits or do not follow the requirements will not be considered during the application review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be reviewed by independent experts; selection will be informed by CZI core values (people, technology, collaboration, open science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI will use review data to select grantee institutions, will not provide feedback to unfunded proposals, and reserves the right to not recommend funding of any application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, deliverables, and participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For awarded projects, financial statements and progress reports are due at the conclusion of each grant year; Imaging Scientists must participate in regular meetings including annual scientist meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deliverable requirements will be outlined in award notification. Travel support for these meetings will be provided separately from requested grant funds. Unused funds may be carried over and no-cost extension requests will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and human/animal subjects requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees should adopt procedures for the use of animals and for ethical treatment of human subjects and tissue donors, including obtaining written informed consent, consistent with their own country requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI regards NIH policies as a strong model. Any human tissue consent must permit full sharing of resulting data and tools; exceptions must be identified at application time and may affect success. Discuss challenging consent situations with CZI scientific staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software sharing policy and licensing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Software developed with CZI support must be made publicly available (e.g., on GitHub) and released under a permissive open source license (MIT, BSD 2-Clause, BSD 3-Clause, or Apache v2.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-existing and derivative code should be licensed under the most permissive license possible given prior constraints. Analysis packages must be released through appropriate language-specific package managers (PyPi, Bioconductor, CRAN) with documentation, example data, and interactive demos (e.g., Jupyter notebooks). Use of Docker or similar containers to ensure portability and reproducibility is expected. Software should be archived for long-term preservation and citability when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and content sharing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets curated or generated through the proposal should be made publicly available and easily accessible through an appropriate data repository under an Open Definition conformant license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally datasets would not include personally identifiable information; if they do, consent for sharing should be obtained. Metadata, documentation, and intended use cases should be provided. Preferred content licenses are CC0 or CC BY/CC BY-SA for content requiring attribution. Exceptions may be considered but must be requested at application and may affect success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and protocol dissemination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications related to funded work must be submitted to a preprint server (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv) at or before first submission to a journal; experimental protocols should be made publicly available via a protocol sharing service (e.g., protocols.io).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI requests that publications, preprints, and presentations resulting from the award acknowledge CZI support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and resource sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and reagents developed with funding should be available for rapid dissemination to the community, where possible in accessible community repositories (e.g., Addgene, Jackson Labs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to cell lines, transgenic organisms, plasmids/clones, antibodies, and other reagents, when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property (IP) expectations and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI does not require assignment of ownership of data, published results, or other IP from funded work, but expects permissive licensing where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All newly developed software should be made available under permissive open source licenses. Other technology/IP should be made freely available for academic and non-commercial use; when commercialized, it should generally be subject to non-exclusive commercial licenses that enable broad availability and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted applications will be kept confidential except as necessary for evaluation/compliance or to the extent the application is made public by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successfully funded proposals may be made publicly available and/or shared with other grantees or collaborators. Unfunded proposals remain confidential, but aggregate information (summaries, metrics, types of applicants) may be made public. Application materials will not be returned to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaging core metadata and technical inventory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaging Core Details must include core type (Service Provider/Research Center/Both), modalities (optical, electron, medical, other), counts of users/labs/active users, inventories of up to 25 major imaging machines and tissue preparation equipment with vendor, quantity and relative usage, personnel listings, physical space metrics, and overall core budget metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active individual users defined as those who have used the facility for ≥20 hours over the last year. For machine/tissue equipment entries, use provided relative usage categories: 'a few hours per week', 'a few hours per day', 'many hours per day', 'nonstop'. Provide up to 25 entries where applicable. Enter N/A if not applicable. Complete financial support sections for active and pending grants, institutional support, other, and recharge/users fees (amount collected in 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical constraints on Institutional Approval Form and electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Approval Form must be uploaded as a single PDF and is not designed to support encrypted documents or digital signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign, scan, and upload the PDF. For technical assistance with SMApply, contact support@smapply.io or use the help function in SMApply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines, contact, and non-negotiable policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates provided: portal opens June 4, 2020; applications due July 30, 2020 by 5 p.m. PT; earliest notification Oct 2020; earliest start Jan 1, 2021. Deadline extensions will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For programmatic/administrative questions contact sciencegrants@chanzuckerberg.com. CZI reserves the right to decide eligibility and to not recommend funding regardless of submission.
